tools.name: explain_rule
tools.description: Explains a validation rule code (e.g. BR-DE-15, BR-CO-10, BR-S-08, PEPPOL-EN16931-R008) in German: what the rule requires, how to fix the invoice and which XML element is affected (UBL and CII path). Useful for findings from any validator, e.g. the KoSIT validator. No API key needed, not counted aga

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Returns status, version and rule set of the eRechio API (same as GET /v1/status): structuredContent {status (ok or gestört), version, regeln, regelstand, zeit, gruende}. isError is true while the service is disturbed. No API key needed, not counted against the quota.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "validate_invoice" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "explain_rule" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_invoice · Private data: validate_invoice, explain_rule, get_status · Public sink: validate_invoice.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_invoice · Private data: validate_invoice, explain_rule, get_status · Public sink: validate_invoice

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
